According to data from Counterpoint Research, although global smartphone shipments have declined overall, Apple still accounted for nearly half of global smartphone revenue last quarter (Q2). Details as follows.

Apple Achieves Highest Revenue Share Record in Q2

Counterpoint Research released a new report (cited via MacMagazine) indicating that Apple captured a historic high of 49% of global smartphone revenue last quarter, with year-on-year revenue growth of 22%. This marks the highest revenue share the company has ever recorded for a second quarter.

Counterpoint noted that global smartphone revenue grew 7% year-on-year during the quarter, with Apple posting the fastest growth among the top five brands. Its average selling price rose from US$879 a year ago to US$946.

Apple's shipment share in Q2 also hit a historic high, climbing from 17% a year ago to 21%. However, Apple still ranked second, trailing Samsung, which held a 23% share of global shipments. Shipment shares for the remaining top five brands all declined, with Xiaomi seeing the largest drop — falling from 14% to 11%, with shipments down 26% year-on-year.

Counterpoint pointed out that the entire industry is facing a memory shortage, with multiple smartphone manufacturers forced to raise prices due to rising component costs and tight supply. Pricing of Apple's iPhones has remained largely stable, but Counterpoint expects this situation to change in the coming quarters.
